# Development

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks

Shared tooling lives in the root `pyproject.toml`, so one command covers every
Python project:

```bash
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy apps brand packages
uv run --directory website mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
```

## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

### Conversational UI coverage

The agent-composed surfaces and the first-run tour are covered at these levels:

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.test.ts` | Spec parsing: prop types, enums, ranges, required props, depth/node/size ceilings, unknown types |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.test.tsx` | Card rendering, computed opportunity scores, action dispatch, per-node failure isolation, catalog/registry parity |
| `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.test.tsx` | Prose and surfaces interleaved in the agent's order; card actions become messages |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_ui_spec.py` | Catalog validation and `render_ui` tool-schema generation |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_ui.py` | `render_ui` interception, `ui` SSE events, and the correction fed back to the model |
| `apps/studio/src/features/flags.test.ts` | Flag precedence (query → storage → env → default), value parsing, local overrides |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/machine.test.ts` | Tour transitions, no forward motion without a goal, versioned storage, malformed records |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.test.tsx` | Auto-open, full flow to a destination, skip/Escape, focus trap, resume, replay, inline model repair, flag off |
| `apps/studio/src/App.test.tsx` | First-run ordering: tour over the context conversation, job handoff, chosen surface opens, flag off in shell tests |

## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)

The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
committed OG art is reproducible, that `index.html` stays in sync with the
README, and that the publish pipeline (`website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py`)
still exists:

```bash
uv run --directory website pytest tests/
```

Publishing happens in `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: it runs those tests, builds
`_site` from `website/`, and deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages` on
every push to `main`. There is no `gh-pages` branch, so that workflow is the only
thing that keeps <https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/> online.

## Formatting workflow

- **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
  (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

  ```bash
  uv run ruff format .
  ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
    changes, and push again.

## Pre-commit hooks

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
You can also trigger them manually:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they
cover, and every test runs from the repository root:

```bash
uv run pytest                        # everything
uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
```

The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, so add or change a tool in
both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` aligned
with the same tool names.

## Test Coverage

CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and uploads one combined
`coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job to
[Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi).

The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

- **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
  tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
- **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
  suite catches up.

To reproduce the report locally:

```bash
uv run pytest \
  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
  --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
```

> [!NOTE]
> Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `apps/studio/` and test
> directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.

### Conventions

- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
  `test_*.py`.
- Root `tests/` is reserved for cross-package checks (`contract/` and
  `scripts/`).
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The MCP server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before
  each test.

### Test Coverage Map

| Area | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/tests/` | Domain models, opportunity scoring, `ODIService`, repository implementations, SQLite persistence, schema, and repository factory |
| `apps/mcp-server/tests/` | Full ODI workflow, entity parity, context tools, Customer Outcomes, evidence, tool errors, and HTTP transport startup |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/` | Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough |
| `apps/cli/tests/` | Backend selection, local/remote CRUD, chat, wizard, onboarding, updates, rendering, connectors, and startup performance |
| `packages/connectors/tests/` | Catalog presets, registry persistence, factory, MCP and REST connectors, evidence mapping, and sink |
| `tests/contract/` | Live MCP tool surface and CLI local-handler parity |
| `tests/scripts/` | `scripts/dev.py` startup, port checks, signals, and shutdown |
| `apps/studio/src/**/*.test.ts` | SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client |
| `website/tests/` | Static site integrity, OG art reproducibility, and README sync |

> [!TIP]
> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the
> results automatically.

# Browser BFF for Living Studio

Date: 2026-10-24
Status: Approved

## Problem

The hosted Living Studio depends on a Python sidecar for canvas CRUD, chat, memory,
connectors, and model access. Cloudflare Pages serves the SPA only; without a
reachable sidecar the studio is unusable. We want the hosted studio to be useful
on its own while preserving the richer local experience when a sidecar is running.

## Decision

Add a client-side backend-for-frontend (BFF) inside the SPA. The BFF owns local
data, local memory, capability discovery, and chat orchestration. IndexedDB is the
source of truth for ODI data. The sidecar becomes an optional enhancement provider
for connectors, MCP, CLI integration, and server-side model proxying.

No new hosted server is introduced.

## Architecture

```
React components
  -> StudioContext
    -> StudioBff facade
      -> CapabilityRegistry
      -> LocalDataService  -> LocalStore (IndexedDB, in-memory fallback)
      -> LocalMemoryService ->
      -> ChatOrchestrator -> deterministic local assistant
                           -> browser built-in model (feature detected)
                           -> OpenAI-compatible endpoint (direct fetch)
                           -> sidecar /api/llm/chat (when available)
      -> SidecarEnhancements -> existing /api/* endpoints
```

### Local data

IndexedDB database `agentic-odi-studio` version 1 with stores `meta`, `jobs`,
`steps`, `outcomes`, `observations`, `conversations`, and `turns`. A `LocalStore`
interface isolates persistence so tests use `fake-indexeddb` and browsers without
IndexedDB fall back to an in-memory store for the session.

Domain behavior mirrors `packages/core`: job/step/outcome CRUD, insertion order,
opportunity score `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`, step cascade
on job delete, outcome cascade on step delete, and input validation.

### Capabilities

`CapabilityRegistry` probes and exposes:

| Capability | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| `local-data` | always |
| `local-memory` | always |
| `deterministic-assistant` | always |
| `browser-model` | feature detected |
| `endpoint-model` | configured endpoint URL + model |
| `sidecar-llm` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-connectors` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-mcp` | sidecar capability probe |
| `sidecar-import` | sidecar capability probe |

Enhanced controls are hidden when unavailable. Settings shows a compact status
list and the chat empty state links to it. Toasts/hints explain that running the
local sidecar unlocks connectors and MCP.

### Assistant and memory

`ChatOrchestrator` streams events in the existing SSE shape (`message`, `chunk`,
`tool`, `tool_result`, `ui`, `done`, `error`) so the current conversation UI keeps
working. The deterministic assistant answers common questions about the canvas
and supports core jobs/steps/outcomes plus `remember` and `render_ui`. External
models use the OpenAI-compatible tool loop. Sidecar chat remains available as an
enhancement and for tools that only exist server-side.

Conversation history and observations are stored locally. A one-time import from
the sidecar fills the local store only when it is empty. JSON workspace export and
import are provided; automatic replication and E2EE are deliberately deferred.

### Sidecar

The existing `/api/chat` endpoint is unchanged for other clients. Add:

- `POST /api/llm/chat`: streaming OpenAI-compatible proxy that keeps provider keys
  server-side and avoids browser CORS restrictions.
- `GET /api/capabilities`: capability manifest used by the SPA probe.
- Existing CRUD/memory endpoints remain for import and enhancement use.

### Hosted worker

`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` returns a local-only capability manifest with status
200 when `SIDECAR_URL` is absent. CSP `connect-src` is built from `LLM_ORIGINS`
(defaults limited to localhost plus curated providers) so direct browser model
calls are allowed only where configured.

## Risks

- IndexedDB is origin-scoped. Hosted and desktop origins do not share data; export
  is available for moving a workspace.
- Browser built-in LLM APIs are not universally available. Detection must be
  conservative and the UI must hide the option when absent.
- Direct provider calls expose the user's key to the browser by design; the
  sidecar proxy is the recommended path when available.
- No automatic sync means local and sidecar data can diverge. The one-time import
  and explicit export/import make the boundary visible.

## Acceptance

- The hosted SPA can create and edit canvas data with no sidecar.
- Local data survives reload in an IndexedDB-capable browser.
- The deterministic assistant can read and mutate the canvas.
- Enhanced features stay hidden unless detected; Settings reports why.
- Existing sidecar behavior and Python tests remain green.
- `npm --prefix apps/studio run lint|typecheck|test|build` and `uv run pytest` pass.

@router.post("/llm/chat")
async def proxy_llm_chat(body: LlmProxyRequest) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Proxy a streaming model call so provider keys stay server-side."""
    url = f"{body.base_url.rstrip('/')}/chat/completions"

    async def event_stream():
        headers = {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Accept": "text/event-stream",
        }
        if body.api_key:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {body.api_key}"
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "model": body.model,
            "messages": [message.model_dump() for message in body.messages],
            "stream": body.stream,
        }
        if body.tools:
            payload["tools"] = body.tools

        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60.0) as client:
            try:
                async with client.stream(
                    "POST", url, headers=headers, json=payload
                ) as response:
                    if response.status_code >= 400:
                        text = (await response.aread()).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                        yield (
                            "event: error\n"
                            + f"data: {json.dumps({'error': {'code': 'provider_error', 'message': text or f'HTTP {response.status_code}'}})}\n\n"
                        )
                        return
                    async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
                        yield chunk.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                yield (
                    "event: error\n"
                    + f"data: {json.dumps({'error': {'code': 'provider_error', 'message': str(exc)}})}\n\n"
                )

    return StreamingResponse(
        event_stream(),
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )

## Quick Start

**Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package
manager.

```bash
# Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling)
uv sync --all-packages

# Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together
npm --prefix apps/studio run build
python scripts/dev.py
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
| The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |

For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the
sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use
`npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See
[Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md).

The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an
opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding
the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation
starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and
audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable.

After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the
screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that
mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity
thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet
rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread
instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the
studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the
card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry
signals while you were away**.

The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes
what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders,
evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you
can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the
next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with
`AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if
it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread.

The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support
(see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one:
with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains
editable by hand.

### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio)

Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke.

- **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location
  with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is
  `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See
  [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md).
- **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list,
  remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear,
  GitHub).
- **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector".
  It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the
  preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a
  suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list.
- **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and
  `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors
  `?area=<capability>` and `?recommended=true`).
- **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add <preset> | list | health <name> | ingest <name>`.
